# Referee proof review

**Verdict.** Theorem I is correct for the finite semigroup generated by **nonempty** call words. It is the finite Rees-quotient nilpotence criterion applied to the ideal of rectangular relations. The tie lemma is correct for living families once their common serial set is made an explicit hypothesis. Complement closure alone does not suffice. The asserted label/order classification is false: a comparable pair of core classes need not eliminate conserved labels, and incomparable core classes need not give a conserved endpoint label when transient endpoints are present.

This is an audit only. No lifecycle changes, current-study implementation inspection, network use, or fresh mathematical computation occurred in this lane. The three authorized study notes were read. Earlier referee directories were listed, but their code/data contents were not needed. The examples below were checked by direct algebra. Parent-reported census results are identified separately.

## Theorem I: checked proof and exact scope

Let X be a finite nonempty set, G a nonempty set of generating relations on X, and S the semigroup of products of **positive-length** words over G. All call words and their repetitions must be admitted. A relation is rectangular when it is A x B; the empty relation is included. Forgetting means that some N makes every word of length at least N rectangular. Requiring this only at length N is equivalent, because rectangularity is preserved by multiplication on either side.

For relations U,V,

    U (A x B) V = {x : some a in A satisfies xUa}
                  x {z : some b in B satisfies bVz}.

Consequently I = S intersect Rect is a two-sided ideal whenever nonempty. It may be empty, and need not contain the empty relation unless that relation is generated. The absorption assertion also holds for an empty prefix or suffix, interpreted using the identity relation only for this calculation.

If a nonrectangular idempotent E is R_w for a nonempty word w, then R_(w^k) = E for every k >= 1. These arbitrarily long admitted words disprove forgetting.

Conversely, color each interval (i,j) of a sufficiently long word by its product in S. Finite Ramsey for |S| colors gives i<j<k whose three interval products have the same value e. Associativity gives e^2=e. Thus every sufficiently long word has a nonempty contiguous idempotent factor. If all idempotents lie in I, this factor is rectangular, and the ideal property makes the whole word rectangular. This proves Theorem I. There is no dependence here on complement closure, ties, a cube state set, or a census.

For nonempty proper I, form the Rees quotient Q=S/I, collapsing I to an absorbing zero. Theorem I is exactly:

    all idempotents of S belong to I
      iff Q has no nonzero idempotent
      iff Q is nilpotent (Q^N={0} for some N).

A nonzero idempotent in Q lifts to an idempotent of S outside I, since equality to a nonzero quotient class means equality of the original elements. The finite Ramsey argument proves the last equivalence as well. Nilpotence in Q agrees with eventual rectangularity for generator words: a product of N arbitrary elements of S expands into a generator word of length at least N, and generator words are products in S. If I=S, forgetting is immediate and the quotient is the one-element zero semigroup. If I is empty, the usual nonempty-ideal Rees quotient is unavailable; both forgetting and the all-idempotents condition are false for nonempty finite S. Equivalently one can adjoin a zero before taking the quotient.

**Empty-product warning.** An identity adjoined only for the empty word must not enter the idempotent test. With G={X x X} and |X|>1, every positive word is rectangular, while the empty-word identity is a nonrectangular idempotent. The theorem correctly uses the product semigroup, not an automatically enlarged monoid. A unit actually generated by a positive word is, of course, a valid obstruction.

## The idempotent core: the correct part

For finite E with E^2=E, let C={x:xEx}. On C, x<=y iff xEy is a preorder. Define x~y by xEy and yEx. Then

    E is nonrectangular iff C/~ has at least two classes.

Proof: E is transitive, and E^n=E for every n>=1. Every E pair xEy therefore has arbitrarily long E paths from x to y. A repeated state in a path longer than |X| gives c in C with xEc and cEy. Thus every pair factors through the core. If there is just one core class K, E=A x B, where A is the set of predecessors of K and B the set of successors of K: factorization proves one inclusion and mutual reachability inside K proves the other. If there is no core class then E is empty. Conversely, a nonempty rectangular idempotent A x B has C=A intersect B nonempty and all its core points mutually related.

Finiteness matters: the strict order on the rationals satisfies E^2=E and has an empty core, yet is nonrectangular. This is outside the declared finite scope.

## Endpoint labels: the necessary correction

Here a nontrivial conserved endpoint label means f(x)=g(y) for every xEy, with more than one value occurring on the active supports dom(E), im(E). Values on unused states do not count.

The exact test uses the **classical bipartite incidence graph** of the relation: one left copy of dom(E), one right copy of im(E), and an incidence for each xEy. Every equality f(x)=g(y) is constant on each connected component. Conversely, the component identifier gives such an equality. Hence E has a nontrivial conserved endpoint label **iff this graph has at least two components**. This is a mathematical representation of the relation, with no native-contact interpretation.

Core comparability is a different test. If all core classes are connected by undirected chains of comparabilities, no nontrivial endpoint label exists, because every relation incidence factors through the core. Merely finding one comparable pair does not suffice. Conversely, incomparable core classes can be joined by a common transient predecessor or successor, eliminating a label. On the core restriction alone, the weak components of the core preorder are conserved; extending this label to the full relation is an additional obligation.

If E is reflexive on its active support, the two component tests agree. In that restricted case an antichain of core classes does conserve the class label, and absence of a conserved label requires connectedness of the full comparability graph, not merely one comparable pair. More generally, dom(E)=im(E) together with an antichain of core classes already forces all active states into the core and gives this equivalence-relation case.

**Counterexample A: incomparable core classes, no conserved endpoint label.** Let

    a=000, b=111, c=001, d=110,
    E={(a,a),(b,b)} union ({a,b} x {c,d}),

with all other rows empty. This relation is complement closed. Its two nonempty rows are E(a)={a,c,d} and E(b)={b,c,d}; c,d have no successors. Therefore E^2=E. Its core is {a,b}, with two incomparable singleton classes, and it is nonrectangular because (a,a),(b,b) occur but (a,b) does not. Both starts reach c, so f(a)=g(c)=f(b); all active output labels then have that same value. There is no nontrivial conserved endpoint label. There is also no coordinate tie: each of the two complementary starts reaches the same endpoint c. This example already has a common nonempty living set {a,b}, since both states have loops. Thus livingness does not repair the classification.

**Counterexample B: comparable classes, conserved parity, no coordinate tie.** On all eight cube states let

    P0={000,111}, Q0={001,110},
    P1={010,101}, Q1={011,100},
    E=Delta_X union (P0 x Q0) union (P1 x Q1).

Complement preserves each displayed set. E is reflexive. A nonidentity pair goes from some Pi to Qi, and no Qi has a nonidentity successor. Hence E^2=E. All core classes are singleton, and there are comparable distinct classes. Nevertheless f(x)=x1 xor x2, with coordinates read left to right, is conserved on every pair. Its two values are the two incidence components. There is no coordinate self-tie: the diagonal rules out an opposite tie, and a row from any Pi contains the complementary pair in Qi, ruling out an equality tie for every coordinate. This example has full support and is serial, so transient endpoints cannot explain away this defect.

These examples refute an exhaustive, mutually exclusive division of all finite idempotents into the two asserted cases. They do not refute a census count produced by an explicitly named proxy. A count using “some comparable core classes” can remain arithmetically correct, while its interpretation as “no quantity is conserved” is false. Reporting both the core-comparability test and the full-relation label test preserves the evidence.

## The tie lemma: correct for living families

For a **nonempty** complement-closed relation on two bits, the possibilities are equality, inequality, and the full relation. The empty relation is the fourth complement-closed possibility and must not be silently excluded. A tie in R composes along powers, but its projection has both bit values only when the power is nonempty.

**Counterexample C to the unqualified lemma.**

    R={(000,001),(111,110)}.

R is complement closed, has equality self-ties on its first two coordinates and an opposite self-tie on its third, but dom(R) and im(R) are disjoint. Thus R^2 is empty. The semigroup {R,empty} forgets at length 2 despite containing a self-tie.

The exact sufficient condition for the intended pumping argument is R_w^k nonempty for every k>=1. For a finite relation this is equivalent to R_w containing a directed cycle. A common nonempty G_S on which **each generator is serial** supplies the required condition uniformly: every x in G_S has a successor in G_S under each generator; induction makes every word and every power serial there. Given this premise, powers inherit the self-tie with sign raised to k and inherit complement closure. Nonemptiness plus complement closure supplies both bit values, so each power's projected equality/inequality is nonrectangular. Projection of a rectangular relation is rectangular; hence none of these powers is rectangular and forgetting fails.

The parent reports that this common living-set condition was proved in the permitted earlier referee work and is being freshly checked for the actual generators. The intended family-scoped tie theorem therefore survives; its stated “every finite complement-closed family” scope needs this explicit narrowing. Syntactic permission to repeat a word alone does not establish nonempty relational powers.

Direct controls are consistent: (X x X)^n=X x X forgets; Delta_X^n=Delta_X does not forget for |X|>1. For an example with ordering and no conserved label, partition X into complement-stable nonempty U={000,111}, V=X\U, and use U x U union U x V union V x V. Its square is itself, its two core classes satisfy U<V, and its incidence graph is connected.

## Census evidence and remaining obligations

The independent mathematical proof above validates Theorem I. The reported 0/12,759 is a consistency check on decided census cases, not independent scientific evidence for this theorem. Reusing a prior semigroup engine or its relation encodings leaves shared construction/composition errors untested; a fresh train/held-out salt does not create checker independence. An independent implementation from raw family definitions could provide useful implementation validation, but cannot turn a deterministic theorem consequence into an independent empirical mechanism. Exact implementation provenance and the current census counts belong to the parent's permitted independent computation, not this lane.

The parent reports a concrete held-out mixed case, family 4f5934b2e118: its nonrectangular idempotent is 0x58a01008051a00 (relation bit 8x+y, little-endian integer state coordinates), reached by word [1,1]. It has comparable core classes and conserves parity mask 5. The parent also reports that the strict absence-of-label count is 43/45 held out, whereas the any-comparable proxy reproduces 44/45. These are parent-reported results, not independently recomputed in this proof lane. Counterexamples A and B establish the logical defects independently of those numbers.

The remaining parent-owned obligations are: record the living-set hypothesis and its generator check; state whether every reported label is global or only on the core; replace the exclusive label/order interpretation with the two explicitly computed properties; reconcile the affected census wording/counts and any correction record. No growth, native-contact, canonical-test, or novelty conclusion follows from this review.
